verses.text: Angels were apprehensive of Allah creating humans. They reasoned that humans will create mischief and shed blood. Allah said to the angels: “I know, what you know not”. (SurahAl-Baqarah : Section 4)

Allah taught Adam (a.s) the names of all the things in heaven. Allah then asked the angels the names to which they said that they have no knowledge except what Allah has taught. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)
Adam (a.s) was able to reply all the names, thus sealing his superiority. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)
Allah then says to the angels “I know the secrets of the heavens and the earth and I know what you reveal and what you conceal”. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)
Allah then ordered the angels to prostrate before Adam. All the angels prostrate before Adam (a.s) except Iblees who refused in his arrogance and became a disbeliever. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)
Adam (a.s) was asked to dwell in Paradise with his wife and eat everything, except from one tree. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)

Shaitaan (Iblees) tempted Adam (a.s) and his wife to disobey. Allah asked them to get down from Paradise and earth will be their abode and provision for a certain period. (Surah Al- Baqarah : Section 4)
Allah taught Adam (a.s) duas to repent and Adam (a.s) did, and Allah accepted his repentance, as He is Most Merciful, Acceptor of Repentance. (Surah Al-Baqarah : Section 4)
The example of the birth of Isa a.s (Jesus) in the sight of Allah is like the example of Adam a.s (who had no father or mother). (Surah Al-e-Imran: Section 6)
Story of Adam (a.s)’s two sons. How each offered a sacrifice, and how the offering of one was accepted while that of the other was not. (Surah Al-Ma’idah : Section 5)
The one whose sacrifice was not accepted, killed his brother due to jealousy. (He carried the dead body of his brother and did not know what to do with it). (Surah Al-Ma’idah : Section 5)

Then, Allah sent a raven, which dug the ground to show him how to bury the dead body of his brother. “Alas!” he cried, “I failed even to be like this raven to find some way to dispose the dead body of my brother!”. So he became full of regrets. (Surah Al-Ma’idah : Section 5)

Mention is made of the story of Iblees (or Shaitaan) not prostrating to Adam a.s. When Allah questions Iblees, he replies, “I am better than he; You created me from fire and him from clay”. Iblees was full of pride. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Allah asks him to get down from the heavens and Iblees pleads with Allah for respite until the Day of Resurrection. Allah grants him this request. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)

Iblees, having been humiliated then throws a challenge saying, “I will lie in ambush for mankind. I will come upon them from their front, from their rear, from their right and from their left,and You will not find most of them grateful to You”. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Allah then says: “Get out from here, despicable and outcast; I will certainly fill hell with you and all of them who follow you.” (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Allah addresses Adam a.s saying: “Dwell with your wife in paradise and eat any fruit you please; but never approach this tree or you shall become wrongdoers”. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Iblees seduced them to eat from that tree saying, it would enable them to become angels or immortals. He further swore to them that he was a sincere adviser. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Eating from the tree made the shame of Adam and Hawwa visible to them, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves of the garden. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Allah called out: “Did I not forbid you to approach that tree, anddid I not warn you that Shaitan was your open enemy. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Adam and his wife replied: “O our Rabb! We have wronged our souls. If You do not forgive us and have mercy on us, we shall certainly be of the losers”. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
Allah said to them to get down from heaven, and earth will be their dwelling place and means of livelihood for a fixed term. (Surah Al-A’raf : Section 2)
O children of Adam! Allah has sent down to you clothing tocover your nakedness and as an adornment, however, the best clothing is the clothing of piety. (Surah Al A’raf : Section 3)
Shaitaan and his tribe can see you from where you cannot seethem. They are always waiting to seduce man towards what isshameful. (Surah Al A’raf : Section 3)

The covenant of Alast is explained: After Adam (a.s)’s creation, Allah brought into existence all the offspring from the loins of Adam (virtually every single individual of mankind who would come to earth) and made them to testify that He is their Rabb. (Surah Al A’raf : Section 22)

This was done so man will not have an excuse on the Day of Judgement, that he was unaware that Allah is the Rabb. Or the excuse to say, our forefathers started the practice of shirk and we just followed. (Surah Al A’raf : Section 22)
When Allah ordered all the angels to prostrate before Adam, Iblees refused, saying that it is not appropriate for him toprostrate to this man made of sounding clay. (Surah Al-Hijr : Section 3)
Allah cursed him and asked him to get out of the assembly of angels. (Surah Al-Hijr : Section 3)
At this Iblees requested: “O my Rabb! Give me respite until the Day of Resurrection”. Allah said: “All right! You are given the respite till the Day of appointed time.” (Surah Al-Hijr : Section 3)

Iblees said: “O my Rabb! Since You let me go astray, I will make evil fair-seeming to them on earth and I will seduce them all, except those of them who are Your sincere devotees.” (Surah Al- Hijr : Section 3)

Reminder is given of the incident when Allah asked Iblees to prostrate before Adam and he refused. Allah ordered him to go away, and hell will be the reward for him and for those who follow him. (Surah Al-Isra : Section 7)
Shaitan (or Iblees) tries to allure people with his seductive voice and makes promises to them; the promise of Shaitaan is nothing but deception. (Surah Al-Isra : Section 7)

Reminder of the story of Iblees wherein Allah asked him to prostrate before Adam and he refused. Allah asks us: Would you then take Iblees and his children as your protectors rather than Allah, even though they are your enemies? (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 7)
Allah has given all kinds of examples in this Quran for the people to understand its Message, but man is exceedingly contentious (i.e argues and debates). (Surah Al-Kahf : Section 8)

Allah reminds about the incident when Iblees (or Shaitan) did not prostrate to Adam, and Allah warned: O Adam! This Shaitan is a real enemy to you and to your wife. Do not let him get you both out of Paradise and get you in trouble. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 7)
Shaitaan seduced Adam and his wife saying: “Should I show to you the Tree of Immortality and an everlasting kingdom.” (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 7)

Adam and his wife ended up eating the fruit of the forbidden tree. As a result, their private parts became apparent to them and they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden. (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 7)

Later on Adam repented and his Rabb accepted his repentance and gave him guidance, saying: “Get down from here all of you (Adam, Eve and Iblees); some of you are enemies to one another.” (Surah Ta-Ha : Section 7)

O Prophet, say: “I had no knowledge of the exalted assembly of angels when they were disputing (regarding the creation of Adam a.s). It has been revealed to me, and I am but a clear Warner”. (Surah S’ad : Section 5)

Reminder is made of the story of Adam (a.s)’s creation wherein, Allah ordered all the angels to prostrate before him. All the angels did except for Iblees. He acted arrogantly and became one of the disbelievers. (Surah S’ad : Section 5)
Iblees said: “I swear by Your Honor; I will mislead them all except your chosen sincere devotees among them”. (Surah S’ad : Section 5)
Allah said, “The Truth is, and the Truth I say: that I shall fill hell with you and all of those who follow you among them”. (Surah S’ad : Section 5)
